findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence and descendant credit disagree in direction. Endpoint selection contrasts are strongly positive for pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5 and landmark_00_occupancy3 (endpoint_effects:9-11,15), while the recorded descendant survival credit for the same family is weak and mostly null (survival_effects:0 q=0.12; survival_effects:96 q=0.12; survival_effects:146 q=0.12; survival_effects:156 q=0.16; survival_effects:196 q=0.75; survival_effects:249 q=0.30; survival_effects:286 q=0.30; survival_effects:326 q=0.35; survival_effects:366 q=0.35; survival_effects:396 q=0.30). Because decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, this last-record joint-head credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; the immediate-vs-descendant comparison is unavailable at the terminal-label level and the disagreement should only reorder direction priorities, not establish a quality axis.

Ancestral coverage is thin and survivor bias is material: lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, out of 700 total batch nodes, with only 14 complete-survival batches and 2 teachers per batch maximum. Descendant credit is therefore computed on a small, unevenly covered surviving subset, so the recorded survival enrichment is a survivor-conditioned quantity rather than an unbiased population effect.

Multiplicity-adjusted support and coverage change the ranking relative to point estimates. The pair-kernel family is the only one with both a large integrated endpoint effect and a positive batch fraction of 1.0 at short range (endpoint_effects:9-11, positive_batch_fraction=1.0), and its adjusted branch covariance/correlation entries survive BH at q<0.05 (branch_adjusted:86 q=0.081, branch_adjusted:87 q=0.077, branch_adjusted:163 q=0.027, branch_adjusted:164 q=0.041). By contrast, several larger-magnitude landmark softmin point estimates (e.g. endpoint_effects:14,20,32,68) have positive_batch_fraction 0.0-0.86 and adjusted q values that do not survive, so a point-estimate-only ranking would over-prioritize them.

Independent-batch agreement is high for the short-range pair kernels: same_sign_batch_fraction is 0.786-0.857 for pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5 (branch_adjusted:86,87,88,163,164,165) and positive_batch_fraction is 1.0 in the endpoint table (endpoint_effects:9-11). The counterexample that would weaken this direction is pair_kernel_7.0, which flips sign (endpoint_effects:13 integrated z=-0.485, positive_batch_fraction=0.0; branch_adjusted:167 same_sign_batch_fraction=0.93 with negative mean), so the short-range pair-kernel direction should not be extended to the 7.0 A shell.

Local coordinate information is separable from global pose and shape. The joint innovation, translation and internal RMS diagnostics are the only features with consistently negative adjusted effects and near-unanimous batch agreement (branch_adjusted:74 q=0.038, 75 q=0.095, 76 q=0.044; branch_adjusted:151 q=0.020, 152 q=0.072, 153 q=0.030; branch_adjusted:228 q=9.3e-5, 229 q=0.087, 230 q=1.5e-4; branch_adjusted:305 q=2.8e-4, 306 q=0.052, 307 q=9.7e-4), whereas global centroid and shape entries are mostly null (branch_adjusted:77-85, 231-239). The joint internal fraction is 0.787 of the teacher contrast (joint_diagnostics:14), so the region that adds information beyond common motion is the internal-coordinate component, and the surrounding global translation/rotation coordinates should retain freedom rather than be constrained.

Coherent joint patterns dominate isolated marginals. Innovation-native alignment and teacher-innovation-contrast alignment are positive and significant (joint_diagnostics:1 p=1.5e-9, joint_diagnostics:11 p=1.2e-9), and the internal fraction is 0.787 (joint_diagnostics:14), while the observed child score gain association is negative (joint_diagnostics:2 mean -0.036, positive_batch_fraction 0.0). The joint internal RMS adjusted correlation is the strongest single entry (branch_adjusted:307 mean -0.137, q=9.7e-4), so coupling evidence supports the joint internal pattern rather than any isolated marginal descriptor.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolants over the full observed support [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation_allowed=false for every row, and they show many sign changes (e.g. continuous:0 sign_changes=4, continuous:1 sign_changes=6, continuous:3 sign_changes=10, continuous:49 sign_changes=13, continuous:68 sign_changes=13). Fit fidelity is poor for many: relative_node_RMSE ranges from ~0.28 to ~0.997, and polynomial_accepted is false throughout. A constant rule is therefore not supported by these curves, but neither is a time-conditioned rule with arbitrary bins; only within-support interpolation is permitted, and the contrast curve is not an absolute reward target.

The curve-fidelity audit selects only 24 of the candidate curves under the rule relative_rmse_le=0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq=0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le=0.1, and every selected curve has legendre_runtime_allowed=false. The selected set includes pair_kernel_1.5 (relative_node_rmse 0.483) and pair_kernel_2.5 (0.386) but excludes most landmark softmin/occupancy curves, whose relative_node_rmse is 0.58-0.93 with 1-15 strong sign-conflict nodes. This is a validated-fit criterion, not a causal benefit claim.

Population-contrast changes and parent-child increment contrasts diverge. For landmark_00_local_cxx the population rate is near zero (turnover:12 mean -0.058) while the edge rate is strongly negative (turnover:13 mean -4.34, q=0.055) and the turnover residual is strongly positive (turnover:14 mean 4.29, q=0.038); the same pattern appears for landmark_00_local_cyy (turnover:15-17) and repeatedly across landmarks (turnover:47, 134, 224, 227, 254, 257, 377, 497, 524, 563, 584, 587). Because the turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, this is an accounting diagnostic consistent with changing cohort composition rather than a within-path change or a causal selection effect.

The turnover residual is not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity. Its inferential_scope is stated as a descriptive whole-window rate with independent batches, and the residual is large and positive wherever the edge rate is large and negative, which is the signature of reclassification and parent weighting rather than a physical force. It should be used only as an accounting diagnostic when interpreting the increment contrasts.

The information audit shows the compressed-choice excess fixed-RMS advantage is small (whole_window_mean 0.081 A, CI95 [0.070,0.092]) and the chosen-teacher score correlation is weak (0.102 compressed, 0.064 full), with top4 teacher overlap 0.470. Teacher contrast coherence is 0.812 and sign-calibration cosine 0.973 (joint_diagnostics:4,10), but these are observational within-selector associations, not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor, so they cannot be treated as evidence of neural-module causation or as an absolute reward target.

A testable coordinate intervention expressible within the permitted reward recipes is a short-range pair-kernel/landmark-occupancy regional attention change: observable is the pair_kernel_1.5-3.5 shell density and landmark_00_occupancy3; intended response is a positive shift in the endpoint pointcloud scalar R; target origin is the detached teacher coordinates at the evidence-bound landmark; spatial scale is the 1.5-3.5 A shell with sigma 0.75 A; temporal scale is the observed support [0.0,0.49] with no extrapolation. The discriminating failure condition is a sign flip or loss of batch agreement at the 7.0 A shell (endpoint_effects:13, branch_adjusted:167), which would falsify the short-range specificity. This remains descriptive unless the Designer selects a registered bounded declarative design; the measurable contrast is not itself the target.

hypotheses.claim: Short-range pair-kernel shell density (1.5-3.5 A) is the most reproducible coordinate hypothesis: it has the largest integrated endpoint effects with positive_batch_fraction 1.0, adjusted q<0.05 in the branch-adjusted correlation table, and is among the 24 curves passing the fidelity audit. Priority should exceed that of larger-magnitude but batch-inconsistent landmark softmin point estimates.

Joint internal-coordinate RMS is a second reproducible hypothesis: it is the only family with near-unanimous negative batch agreement and the strongest adjusted correlation, and the internal fraction of 0.787 indicates it carries information beyond common motion. It should be treated as a coupling diagnostic rather than an isolated marginal.

The 7.0 A pair-kernel shell is a counterexample hypothesis: its endpoint effect is negative with positive_batch_fraction 0.0 and its adjusted correlation is negative, so any short-range pair-kernel direction should be tested for failure at this shell before being extended.

A time-conditioned regional attention rule is not supported by the supplied curves: every continuous function is an observed-node linear interpolant with extrapolation disallowed, polynomial fits are rejected, and sign changes are frequent. A constant rule is also unsupported. Only within-support interpolation of validated curves could express a temporal hypothesis.

The observed population-contrast changes are more consistent with changing cohort composition than with within-path change, because the turnover residual is large and positive wherever the edge rate is large and negative. This remains an accounting diagnostic and does not establish a causal selection effect.

The immediate-vs-descendant disagreement cannot be resolved at the terminal-label level because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable; the recorded descendant credit is joint-head credit on a survivor-biased subset with thin ancestral coverage, so it should only reorder direction priorities and not be presented as final affinity benefit.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling; it is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis are permitted.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; moment effects and pair kernels are diagnostic evidence only.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.
